feeds.title: Society for Historical Archaeology
feeds.description: Historical Archaeology is the study of the material remains of past societies that also left behind documentary and oral histories. This subfield of archaeology studies the emergence, transformation, and nature of the Modern World. The main focus of the society is the era since the beginning of European exploration.

feeds.title: World Archaeology
feeds.description: Current World Archaeology, Britain's most popular world archaeology magazine, tells you about the archaeology of the whole world - from the first emergence of man down to the present day. CWA was founded in 2003 as a sister magazine to Current Archaeology, the biggest magazine devoted to British archaeology which, since 1967, has been reporting on the latest discoveries in British archaeology.

feeds.title: ScienceDaily News » Archaeology
feeds.description: Archaeology News. Read about the latest archaelogical finds including Roman coins, Egyptian pyramids and more. Articles and photos.

feeds.title: Archaeology Southwest
feeds.description: For three decades, Archaeology Southwest has practiced a holistic, conservation-based approach to exploring the places of the past. We call this Preservation Archaeology. By exploring what makes a place special, sharing this knowledge in innovative ways, and enacting flexible site protection strategies, we foster meaningful connections to the past.

feeds.title: MSU Campus Archaeology Program
feeds.description: MSU Campus Archaeology is a program that works to mitigate and protect the archaeological resources on Michigan State University's beautiful & historic campus. Our primary focus is on the MSU community, educating them about their cultural heritage, & how archaeology can be used to discover a community's past. Read posts from members of the Campus Archaeology Program; including the director, the campus archaeologist, graduate students, & undergraduate interns.

feeds.title: Archaeology News
feeds.description: Archaeology News is an international online magazine that covers all aspects of archaeology. As a magazine dedicated to the world of archaeology, it brings you the latest updates, insightful education, and a wealth of resources that delve into the fascinating realm of archaeological discoveries.

feeds.title: The Archaeology Channel - Audio News from Archaeologica
feeds.description: Explore the human cultural heritage through streaming media. Travel through time and feed the thrill of discovery. Examine the wonderful diversity of the human experience!

feeds.title: Archaeological News
feeds.description: The latest news in Archaeology.

feeds.title: Archaeology Orkney
feeds.description: This Blog has been created by The Archaeology Institute, University of the Highlands and Islands in beautiful Orkney. We aim to add features and news about our work on the islands and further afield on a regular basis.

feeds.title: Gambler's House
feeds.description: This blog mainly as a place to synthesize and present my thoughts about Chaco Canyon.

feeds.title: Archaeology News Report
feeds.description: Archaeology News Report blog by Jonathan Kantrowitz.

feeds.title: Ancient Pages » Archaeology News
feeds.description: Stay updated with the latest archaeology news. We provide you with the latest top archaeological finds from all across the world. Ancient Pages is one of the world's largest sites covering all about the ancient world.

feeds.title: Current Archaeology
feeds.description: Covers the archaeology of all periods - from prehistory and ancient human origins, Roman and Anglo-Saxon Britain, and the Middle Ages right through to modern times. Current Archaeology is the UK's only independent consumer magazine aimed at archaeology enthusiasts.

feeds.title: Archaeology Review
feeds.description: Get your daily cup of archaeology, anthropology, science, and skepticism here.

feeds.title: Wessex Archaeology News
feeds.description: Wessex Archaeology is the UK's leading provider of archaeological and heritage services, and an educational charity. Read their Wessex Archaeology news blog for the latest archaeology news, information on projects and recent discoveries, as well as community events and company news.

feeds.title: Looting Matters
feeds.description: Discussion of the archaeological ethics surrounding the collecting of antiquities and archaeological material by David. David Gill is Professor of Archaeological Heritage and Director of Heritage Futures at the University of Suffolk

feeds.title: Project Archaeology Blog
feeds.description: Project Archaeology uses archaeological inquiry to foster understanding of past and present cultures, improve social studies and science education. In this blog, they will cover new events, updates, curriculum, and more.

feeds.title: NOSAS Archaeology Blog
feeds.description: The North of Scotland Archaeological Society (NOSAS) is a group of professional and amateur archaeologists in the Highlands of Scotland. The NOSAS Blog aims is to publish a range of articles relating to the archaeology of the north of Scotland, contributed by authors from both the NOSAS membership and the wider archaeological community. Keep with the latest research, digs, surveys, field trips, and more.

feeds.title: archaeologytea
feeds.description: Covers a wide variety of archaeological topics including industrial archaeology, buildings archaeology, church archaeology, contemporary archaeology, climate change and heritage, community archaeology, and the archaeology of the Manchester area. Dr. Mike Nevell is a landscape, buildings, community, and industrial archaeologist with more than 30 years of experience.

feeds.title: Biblical Archaeology Society
feeds.description: The Biblical Archaeology Society (BAS) was founded in 1974 as a nonprofit, nondenominational, educational organization dedicated to the dissemination of information about archaeology in the Bible lands. BAS educates the public about archaeology and the Bible through its bi-monthly magazine, Biblical Archaeology Review, an award-winning web site, books and DVDs, and tours and seminars.

feeds.title: Almost Archaeology
feeds.description: Almost Archaeology is a daughter page of Love Archaeology Magazine, created by former editor Adrián Maldonado. The mission is to find meaning in pop culture archaeology and explore the materality of pop culture.

feeds.title: The Guardian » Archaeology
feeds.description: Latest news and features from theguardian.com about Archaeology.

feeds.title: Prehistoric Archaeology Blog
feeds.description: The Prehistoric Archaeology Blog is concerned with news reports featuring Prehistoric period archaeology. If you wish to see news reports for general European archaeology, please go to The Archaeology of Europe Weblog.

feeds.title: This Week In Pennsylvania Archaeology
feeds.description: The Section of Archaeology at The State Museum of Pennsylvania curates the largest collection in the museum and is responsible for multiple functions within the PHMC. Developing and maintaining exhibits in the Hall of Anthropology and Archaeology is a primary function, but our role as the state repository for cultural resource projects is substantial.

feeds.title: Abydos Archaeology Blog
feeds.description: Abydos Archaeology is the online journal of the North Abydos Expedition sponsored by New York University's Institute of Fine Arts and Princeton University. We tell the story of Abydos, Egypt, and its 5,000-year history through archaeological excavation, site preservation, survey & mapping, collections management, object conservation, educational outreach, and publication.

feeds.title: Theoretical Structural Archaeology
feeds.description: Structural archaeologist Geoff Carter's radical view of building in the ancient world, especially the archaeology of the lost timber built environment of Southern England.

feeds.title: Paths Unwritten Blog
feeds.description: Paths Unwritten seeks to discover, document, and share historical, cultural, and practical travel information from the ruins and monuments of ancient kingdoms and civilizations around the world, along with any stray curiosities found on the way.

feeds.title: Roman Archaeology Blog
feeds.description: The Roman Archaeology Blog is concerned with news reports featuring Roman period archaeology. If you wish to see news reports for general European archaeology, please go to The Archaeology of Europe Weblog.

feeds.title: Iowa Archaeology
feeds.description: Representing the University of Iowa Office of the State Archaeologist, a nationally recognized archaeological research center, and the Iowa Archeological Society.

feeds.title: Adventures in Archaeology
feeds.description: Follow our international ArchaeoSpain teams as they excavate and explore ancient sites in Spain and Italy.

feeds.title: UCD Archaeological Society
feeds.description: The Archaeological Society is run by students for students. The society is still dedicated to running numerous events throughout the year and is focused on promoting Archaeology as a subject, helping its members build networks both personally and professionally.

feeds.title: ArchaeoFam
feeds.description: Historical investigators, archaeological adventurers and cultural sector enthusiasts, our little Archaeofam scout the country exploring the most intriguing historical mysteries and archaeological puzzles.

feeds.title: Roman Archaeology Blog
feeds.description: The Roman Archaeology Blog is concerned with news reports featuring Roman period archaeology. Follow us for regular updates from this blog.

feeds.title: Anglo-Saxon Archaeology Blog
feeds.description: The Anglo-Saxon Archaeology Blog is concerned with news reports featuring Anglo-Saxon period archaeology. Follow us for the latest updates from this feed.

feeds.title: Viking Archaeology Blog
feeds.description: The Viking Archaeology Blog is concerned with news reports featuring Viking period archaeology. It was primarily constructed as a source for the University of Oxford Online Course in Viking Archaeology. Follow us for regular updates.

feeds.title: Archaeology In Europe
feeds.description: Archaeology in Europe is run by David Beard MA, FSA, FSA Scot. David Beard is a freelance archaeologist & a Fellow of the Society of Antiquaries & a Fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of Scotland specializing in medieval archaeology, especially the Anglo-Saxon & Viking periods. Here you can find a calendar of archaeological events, including training digs, educational resources for archaeology, and information about archaeological study tours.

feeds.title: Archaeology Fantasies
feeds.description: Archaeology Fantasies where Archaeology and Reality Meet! main goal of this blog is to increase public awareness of archaeology, debunking pseudo-archaeology, and make the field more accessible to the public.

feeds.title: Stone Pages News
feeds.description: Stone Pages Archaeo News is the leading resource for extensive and timely information about the most recent archaeological meetings, digs and breathtaking discoveries, mainly related to prehistoric and megalithic monuments. The Stone Pages is also the first online guide to European megaliths (including Stonehenge) and provides images, descriptions, folklore, panoramic views, forums, weblinks and tours.

feeds.title: Doug's Archaeology
feeds.description: A blog by Doug Rocks-Macqueen. This is my blog were I focus mainly on the Profession of Archaeology e.g. pay, working conditions, career prospect, etc. Though, I do on occasion throw in some other topics and some bits on Open Access.

feeds.title: Publishing Archaeology
feeds.description: This blog contains information and opinions (mostly mine) on professional publishing issues in archaeology. Michael is an archaeologist who works on Aztec sites and Teotihuacan. He do comparative and transdisciplinary research on cities, and also households, empires, and city-states.

feeds.title: Sexy Archaeology
feeds.description: SexyArchaeology.org is owned and maintained by Kurt Thomas Hunt, an archaeologist with a passion for furthering public interest in his field of study. Sexy Archaeology seeks to generate interest in archaeology by seizing upon the image that popular media has created of archaeologists; that of brave, adventurous, attractive and intelligent men and women.

feeds.title: Bone Broke
feeds.description: Posts on Archaeology, Osteology & Biological Anthropology by Jess Beck. Jess Beck's research focuses on the Late Prehistoric period in Europe, a time of significant cultural change.

feeds.title: Northwest Coast Archaeology
feeds.description: Blog post covers interesting news items and commentary on Northwest Coast Archaeology. The goal is to encourage public knowledge about, and appreciation of, Northwest Coast Archaeology through examples of interesting finds and sites, or through commentaries on archaeology in the news or otherwise in the public domain.

feeds.title: Archaeology Magazine
feeds.description: Each bi-monthly issue brings the latest archaeology news and discoveries to more than 730,000 readers. The Archaeology website features daily news from around the world, reports from current excavations, and exclusive online interviews, reviews, and features. A publication of the Archaeological Institute of America.

feeds.title: American Journal of Archaeology
feeds.description: The AJA, a publication of the Archaeological Institute of America, is one of the world's most distinguished and widely distributed classical archaeology journals.

feeds.title: Colleen Morgan
feeds.description: Research in digital archaeology, heritage, and marginalia

feeds.title: Ancient Origins
feeds.description: News and articles relating to ancient human origins, archaeology, anthropology, scientific mysteries, sacred writings, ancient places and more.

feeds.title: Archaeology Data Service Blog
feeds.description: The archaeology data service (ads) supports research, learning and teaching with high quality and dependable digital resources. it does this by preserving digital data in the long term, and by promoting and disseminating a broad range of data in archaeology. the ads promotes good practice in the use of digital data in archaeology.

feeds.title: Rogers Archaeology Lab
feeds.description: A blog by Dr. J. Daniel Rogers - currently a Curator of Archaeology at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History. He is well known for his archaeological work with the Spiro Mounds in Oklahoma and other sites in the southeastern United States and has studied the rise of chiefdoms and empires across the world. Come visit his blog for stories about amazing artifacts, current research, and more.

feeds.title: Rubicon Archaeology
feeds.description: Rubicon Heritage Services Ltd is an archaeological and heritage consultancy firm serving the UK and Irish markets.

feeds.title: Global Archaeology Blog
feeds.description: A blog by Dr. Kate, An archaeologist spending 2016 making her way across the globe contributing her time to archaeological excavations and research projects. Dr. Kate will lend an experienced helping hand to exciting archaeological projects and explore the world while uncovering the past and documenting the journey.
